Sorry this is a little short notice but I think still open for self-registration at link below. There is an NSF grant webinar at 2PM EST today 19NOV24. Details:

Subject: New program deadline and webinar: Artificial Intelligence, Formal Methods, and Mathematical Reasoning

A new deadline and informational webinar for the solicitation NSF 24-554: Artificial Intelligence, Formal Methods, and Mathematical Reasoning (AIMing) is now available.
The AIMing program seeks to support research at the interface of innovative computational and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and new strategies/technologies in mathematical reasoning to automate knowledge discovery. Successful projects should demonstrate the potential to advance both the mathematical sciences as well as the computational models and methods used to attain these advances. This may include, but is not limited to: advancing AI for mathematical conjecture, proof, verification; advancing interactive theorem provers for mathematical proof and verification; developing training data for AI algorithms for mathematical reasoning, both deterministic and under uncertainty; or novel approaches for infusing logic, mathematical reasoning, and compositionality into AI. This is a joint program involving NSF's Divisions of Mathematical Sciences (MPS/DMS), Computing and Communication Foundations (CISE/CCF), and Information and Intelligent Systems (CISE/IIS).

An informational webinar will be held on Tuesday, November 19, 2024 at 2:00 pm Eastern Time. For more details and a link to the registration page visit https://new.nsf.gov/events/artificial-intelligence-formal-methods-mathematical/2024-11-19.
The next proposal deadline is: Wednesday, February 5, 2025.
Questions about the AIMing program should be directed to: aiming@nsf.gov.

Here is the solicitation. Requires a PI who is a tenured professor at a US campus:

https://new.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/aiming-artificial-intelligence-formal-methods-mathematical/nsf24-554/solicitation
